WWII veteran who helped liberate Dachau gets France's highest honour at 102
content: At 102 years old, William Lyford received France's prestigious Legion of Honor, honoring his bravery during World War II, particularly his role in liberating Dachau concentration camp in 1945. The touching ceremony held in Woodstock was filled with family, friends, and fellow veterans celebrating his significant contributions. Despite his service, Lyford’s daughter shared how he rarely discussed his military past, showcasing the lasting bond between the U.S. and France.

title: Debt, dues and deja vu: How poor nations end up paying more than they borrow
content: In 2025, low and middle-income countries are grappling with an alarming spike in external debt, hitting a staggering $9.4 trillion. Alongside this, debt repayment burdens surged to $1.4 trillion, largely due to escalating borrowing rates and a scarcity of new financial support. Nations receiving IDA funding are particularly strained, facing average interest rates of 8.2 percent.

title: 103-year-old D-Day veteran gets wartime medals back after 80 years
content: Douglas Halley, a 103-year-old D-Day veteran, recently received his wartime medals which were lost in 1945. A young historian, Joseph Smith, discovered Halley's military record while researching veterans' stories and assisted in recovering the medals. The Ministry of Defence located and mailed the medals back to Halley just before Remembrance Day. This story highlights the importance of remembering personal histories and the sacrifices of war.
